PLAN "12-Week Metabolic Reset: Fat Loss & Glycaemic Control"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Improve insulin sensitivity and reduce body fat"
  GOAL secondary endurance:
    name "Build cardiovascular capacity for glycaemic control"
  GOAL tertiary habit:
    name "Establish consistent training and nutrition behaviours"

NUTRITION
  STRATEGY "Diabetic-Optimised Fat Loss"
  CALORIES 1600..1750 kcal daily
  MACROS
    protein 130..145 g daily note "Preserve lean mass, blunt postprandial glucose spikes"
    carbohydrate 130..150 g daily note "Low-moderate carb; prioritise low-GI sources only"
    fat 60..75 g daily note "Emphasise mono- and polyunsaturated fats"
    fibre 30..35 g daily note "Critical for glucose blunting and satiety"
  MEAL_TIMING
    meal 1 "Breakfast 07:00" note "Never skip; stabilises fasting glucose. Example: 3-egg omelette with spinach and feta, 1 slice rye toast, black coffee or green tea"
    meal 2 "Pre-training snack 10:00 if training at 11:00" note "Only if training within 60-90 min. Example: 150g Greek yoghurt (plain, full-fat) with 10 almonds. Do NOT train fasted — metformin + exercise raises hypoglycaemia risk"
    meal 3 "Lunch 13:00" note "Largest carb meal of day, post-training window. Example: 150g grilled salmon, 150g roasted sweet potato, large green salad with olive oil and lemon"
    meal 4 "Afternoon snack 16:00" note "Protein-anchored to prevent 4pm glucose dip. Example: 100g cottage cheese, cucumber sticks, 1 tbsp pumpkin seeds"
    meal 5 "Dinner 19:00" note "Low-carb anchor meal. Example: 180g chicken thigh or lean beef, 200g roasted non-starchy vegetables (broccoli, courgette, peppers), 1 tbsp olive oil"
  DIABETIC_NOTES
    note "Monitor blood glucose before and 2 hours after every training session for first 4 weeks"
    note "Target pre-exercise BGL 6.0..10.0 mmol/L. If below 5.5 mmol/L, consume 15g fast carb before training"
    note "Carry 15g fast-acting carbohydrate (4 glucose tablets or 150ml orange juice) to every session"
    note "Avoid alcohol — impairs hepatic glucose output and interacts with metformin"
    note "Hydration target 2.5..3.0 L water daily; dehydration worsens insulin resistance"
    note "Prioritise low-GI carbohydrates: oats, lentils, chickpeas, sweet potato, rye bread, basmati rice"
    note "Avoid refined carbohydrates, sugary drinks, fruit juice, white bread, and processed cereals"
    note "Post-exercise meal within 45 minutes to replenish glycogen and blunt cortisol-driven glucose rise"
    note "Physician review of metformin dosage recommended at week 4 and week 12 as fitness improves"

Do not add fasted cardio. This client is a type 2 diabetic on metformin. Fasted cardio is contraindicated: metformin combined with exercise in a fasted state elevates hypoglycaemia risk, impairs hepatic glucose output recovery, and increases the likelihood of lactic acidosis under prolonged exertion without substrate availability. The existing NUTRITION block explicitly flags this with a pre-exercise BGL check and mandatory pre-training snack protocol. Adding fasted cardio sessions would directly conflict with those safety rules and could cause a medical incident. The programme as written is the correct and safe prescription for this client.

There are no fasted cardio days in this programme. As stated, fasted cardio is contraindicated for this client due to her type 2 diabetes and metformin use. The question presupposes a condition that does not exist in her plan and should not be created.

If the trainer wishes to discuss safe pre-training nutrition timing for this client, that is already specified in the NUTRITION block under meal 2: a small protein-and-fat-anchored snack 60 to 90 minutes before any training session, with a mandatory pre-exercise blood glucose check.

1. 150g plain Greek yoghurt with 10 almonds and a small handful of blueberries
2. 2 hard-boiled eggs with cucumber slices and a rice cake
3. 100g cottage cheese with cherry tomatoes and pumpkin seeds
4. A small protein shake made with water and 25g whey isolate, paired with a small apple
5. 2 tbsp peanut butter on 1 slice rye bread
6. 100g smoked salmon with cucumber and 2 rye crispbreads
7. A small handful of mixed nuts with a low-sugar protein bar (check label: under 5g sugar, over 15g protein)

All options are low-GI, protein-anchored, and appropriate for a type 2 diabetic on metformin. Each should be consumed within 45 minutes post-session as specified in the programme nutrition block. Portions are calibrated to fit within her 1600 to 1750 kcal daily target without displacing a main meal.

Cheat meals are not a recommended construct for this client and should not be built into her programme. The reasons are clinical, not preferential.

Her HbA1c is 7.2, which means glycaemic control is not yet stable. A weekly unstructured high-calorie, high-GI meal will cause acute postprandial glucose spikes, undermine the progressive HbA1c reduction the programme is designed to achieve, interact unpredictably with metformin dosing, and erode the low-GI dietary pattern that is the nutritional foundation of her plan.

The appropriate alternative is a structured flexible meal, not a cheat meal. Once per week, after week 4 when her glucose monitoring data shows stable pre and post-exercise readings, she may include one higher-enjoyment meal that still respects the following constraints: no refined sugar, no sugary drinks, no white refined carbohydrates, alcohol excluded, total meal carbohydrate under 60g, and protein present in the meal to blunt glucose response. Examples would be a restaurant grilled fish with roasted vegetables, or a homemade burger in a rye bun with a side salad.

If the trainer wants this formalised in the plan, a NUTRITION note can be added to Phase 2 onward reflecting this flexible meal protocol. Confirm and the DSL block will be emitted.

Intermittent fasting is not recommended for this client and should not be added to her programme. The reasons are clinical.

Metformin taken without food increases the risk of gastrointestinal distress and, in extended fasting windows, contributes to hypoglycaemia risk, particularly around training sessions.
